summary: Host only; nothing flashed or run on the phone in this task and no XNU jump. Native run 005 (decision 0013, loader-diag-trig-hold-adt8) was decoded from the owner's recording (native-attempt-005-evidence.json, outcome fail): the loader reached MEM, ZERO and COPY and then reported SLOT 4, ESR 0x96000061, ELR 0x800a9954, FAR 0x9e2d743fc from inside the loader. Host analysis: loader base 0x800a0000, ELR = `stur x19, [x11, #0x24]` in adt_set_dram+0x268 (64-bit store of the `dram-size` ADT value), FAR - 1020 = the 16 KiB-aligned ADT copy; ADT property values are only 4-byte aligned and the loader runs with the MMU off (Device memory, natural alignment required), so the store is an alignment fault (EC 0x25, DFSC 0x21). The NAT-026 pre-check ran adt_patch.c on x86-64 and could not see it. NAT-027: patch_loader.py --adt-aligned (anchored on the base adt_patch.c SHA-256 415bf5c0...) replaces the five 64-bit ADT property accesses with two aligned 32-bit accesses; build.py adds loader-diag-trig-hold-adt8-aln (build-006): loader Image f0e61342..., Image.payload 2fb3968787688f4feb5b1dc09e4622309f1e22e5e8d76c82178d8716f1642da9 (21767776 bytes), RECOVERY package-006 cdf4f3a15831fb7c6c488085da33c12ade231460323583fd4090114945b285cd. All seven earlier images and payloads (the run-005 image included) keep their hashes; the new image is reproducible (build-006-repro and a rebuild at the commit). check_payload.py gained a gcc alignment-trap run of the real adt_patch.c: the run-005 source FIRES (MISALIGNED ACCESS in adt_set_dram), the aln source passes; scan_unaligned.py finds 4 misaligned unscaled accesses in the run-005 loader (one is the faulting instruction) and 0 in the aln loader; the aligned accessors write byte-identical ADT bytes for window bases below and above 4 GiB (test_nat022.py, 35 tests); make check passes (214 tests). session_aln.py is gated on docs/decisions/0014-nat022-loader-diag-trig-hold-adt8-aln-single-run-2026-11-10.md, which does not exist; without it the driver stops before any device command. Not shown by this evidence: that the later loader stages (ADT patch, boot_args, full-window cache clean, PRE_JUMP hold) run on the S24; other Device-memory alignment hazards outside adt_patch.c (the static scan covers unscaled immediates only; addresses computed at run time are not seen); the RAM window; any XNU entry.
